hook.text: Hold your nose and eat a jellybean—you can't tell the flavor. Release your nose and flavor floods in. 80% of flavor is smell.

buildup.text: Taste detects 5 basic sensations on the tongue. Smell detects over 10,000 distinct odors through receptors in the nasal cavity.

discovery.text: Retronasal olfaction—smelling from inside the mouth while chewing—is the primary flavor mechanism.

twist.text: Smell Defines Flavor has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: People with anosmia (no sense of smell) experience food as bland and unsatisfying.

punchline.text: Flavor lives in your nose, not your tongue. Without smell, all food is flat.

quiz.question: What percentage of perceived flavor comes from smell?
